title: Binance hack: developing story
summary: The largest crypto theft on record: on Oct 29 attackers moved about US$6.3 billion (Binance's estimate) out of Binance's own hot wallets on 10 blockchains. About US$3 billion has been frozen. Binance said on Nov 1 that about 95% of the stolen amount has been replenished from company funds (up from about 90% on Oct 31) and reopened withdrawals on Sunday in stages, Bitcoin first; all 15 first-phase networks were open by 7:36 a.m. ET, with other networks to come after security checks. Binance said net withdrawals were about US$3.64 billion in the first nine and a half hours. On Nov 2 a Binance spokesperson told Reuters net withdrawals since the Sunday restart had reached US$4.72 billion, about 2.8% of assets on the platform, and that withdrawals were slowing; Circle said it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC. On Nov 1 the FBI formally blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group. Its latest update says the full zero-knowledge proof of reserves will be ready by Tuesday, Nov 3 (UTC), a day later than the co-CEO first said, because it takes 40 to 50 hours to compute.

facts.label: Stolen
facts.note: Binance's own estimate of the impact (Reuters); TRM Labs: about US$6.36B moved out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains; Chainalysis's Jonathan Levin put it at US$6.4B in a later update (Cointelegraph, 05:01 UTC Oct 30)
facts.source: Reuters via Investing.com; Cointelegraph live updates

facts.label: Frozen so far
facts.note: Binance said verified frozen assets reached about US$3B (00:52 UTC Oct 30), including more than US$1.567B USDT frozen by Tether and more than US$800M USDC by Circle; First Digital froze the FDUSD involved; on Nov 2 Circle said it had frozen more than US$1.1B in USDC (Reuters via Business Recorder)

facts.label: Still with the attacker
facts.note: Bitquery's count of the attacker's wallets, mostly ether and bitcoin (06:43 UTC Oct 30; Euronews reported US$3.1B from an earlier count). A different measure, TRM Labs' funds 'beyond the reach of token issuers', was about US$2.4B (00:30 UTC Oct 30). Stolen, frozen and still held come from different sources and times, so they need not add up

facts.label: Recovered
facts.value: about 95% of the stolen amount replenished (Binance, Nov 1); no recovered amount published
facts.note: Binance said on Nov 1 that about 95% of the impacted amount is now covered, up from about 90% on Oct 31, with less-liquid tokens outside the top 10 making up the remaining 5% (The Defiant; Business Today; Coinpedia). It has begun recovering frozen funds but has not said how much has come back

facts.label: When
facts.note: most of the money left within about 20 minutes (TRM Labs; Yahoo Finance), and the attacker kept moving funds out of 17 hot wallets until about 7:56 p.m. ET (Bitquery, via Euronews). The first public signs came about an hour after it began: Changpeng Zhao's post at about 5:15 p.m. ET, then Binance's statement

facts.label: Who
facts.value: North Korea's TraderTraitor, a Lazarus-linked unit (FBI, Nov 1)
facts.note: The FBI formally attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group in a public alert on Nov 1, saying it stole more than US$6 billion and is converting the coins mainly into ether (RTE; ABC News Australia; Newsweek; Fox Business). TRM Labs and Chainalysis had reached the same assessment on Oct 30; North Korea routinely denies such attacks

facts.label: Binance
facts.value: deposits working normally; withdrawals restarting in stages: all 15 networks in the first phase (including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Tron, Solana and XRP Ledger) reopened by 7:36 a.m. ET Nov 1, though most listed coins were still suspended; other networks to follow after security checks, no timeline given; full zero-knowledge proof of reserves now due by Tuesday Nov 3 (UTC), after co-CEO Richard Teng had promised it by Nov 2; says it will cover all losses with company funds
facts.note: Bitcoin reopened first (Binance statement via TechFlow, 06:25 UTC Nov 1; crypto.news). ETH, USDT, USDC and BNB withdrawals followed later on Nov 1 (Crypto Briefing; Tech-ish, which timed it at 07:49 UTC). Preliminary finding: a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop let an attacker reach a service container that could submit withdrawal transactions; no evidence of a private-key leak. Binance later found additional points of breach: co-CEO Richard Teng said on Oct 30 the attackers used a self-destruct mechanism to erase their tools and traces and used EIP-7702 to gain execution authority over one hot wallet, bypassing the usual approvals, and that the attack hit Binance's own hot wallet, not customer funds. Binance has reserved more than US$6.34B, US$5B of it already held in the affected assets, the rest being bought on the market and over the counter. Binance.US not affected. Proof of reserves: Binance's latest updates put the full zero-knowledge proof (snapshot taken Oct 31) by Tuesday, Nov 3 (crypto.news, 08:01 UTC Nov 1; Cryptonews.net citing Binance's third update, Oct 31). XRP was also in the first phase (CoinDesk, 10:35 UTC Nov 1; CBS News, which listed XRP among assets restored as of 5 a.m. ET). Bloomberg (via Insurance Journal, 12:40 UTC Nov 1) confirmed the restart, with Bitcoin withdrawals reopening after 2 p.m. Singapore time, and reported that Binance updated its proof-of-reserves wallet list with newly generated addresses that will process all future withdrawals. First phase complete: The Block (11:44 a.m. ET Nov 1) reported all 15 first-phase networks reopened by 7:36 a.m. ET, while 531 of 552 listed coins were still suspended as of 11:22 a.m. ET; Cointribune lists the 15 networks. Binance said US$4.65B was withdrawn and US$1.01B deposited from 1 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. ET Sunday, net outflows of about US$3.64B, which it put at 2.1% of its US$171B in assets (Binance on X, via The Block). The Block put the proof-of-reserves report on Monday; Cointribune on Tuesday, Nov 3. Binance's third recovery update moved the proof to Nov 3 (UTC), citing 40 to 50 hours of computation (Bitcoin.com News, 3:30 a.m. ET Nov 2; Brad Feld, Nov 2). Nov 2: a Binance spokesperson told Reuters net withdrawals since the Sunday restart were US$4.72B (about 2.8% of platform assets), with US$2.7B of inflows, and that withdrawals were stabilising (Business Recorder).
facts.source: The Block; Cointribune; crypto.news; Crypto Briefing
